# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

# Choose an agent integration

> Pick a built-in Weave integration for your agent SDK or harness and start sending conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls to the Agents view.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/get-started/integrations.md).

W\&B Weave traces multi-turn agents built with popular SDKs and harnesses without hand-instrumenting each turn. Install a plugin for your agent harness, or call `weave.init()` in code that uses a supported agent SDK, and Weave autopatches the framework. Conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls render in the **Agents** view of your project.

Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own, because the harness owns the session. Agent SDKs run one turn per call, so your code decides which turns belong to the same conversation. For those integrations, `weave.init()` alone isn't enough.

Choose from one of the following supported integrations.

The following sections describe each top-level tracing function and the arguments it accepts. Use them to instrument the conversation, turn, LLM call, and tool call layers of the data model described in the previous section.

Weave exposes the following top-level functions. Each function returns an object that works as a context manager (using `with` in Python, or `try/finally` in TypeScript) or that you can close manually by calling `.end()`.

## Custom agents and OpenTelemetry

If your agent isn't built with one of the SDKs above, or it already emits OpenTelemetry spans, use the Weave SDK directly. Weave accepts any OTel span and gives special handling to [GenAI semantic-convention attributes](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/) so spans render in the **Agents** view:

* [Quickstart: Manually instrument an agent](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/custom-agents-quickstart.md) — a walkthrough of a small multi-turn agent.
* [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md) — the full reference of agent helpers and concepts.
* [Send OpenTelemetry spans to the Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents-otel.md) — point an existing OTel pipeline at the Weave agents endpoint, with no Weave SDK required.

candidate.answer:
No. `@weave.op` alone won't give you the Agents view. The docs treat `@weave.op` as a separate workflow: it traces individual functions as Ops (tracked function calls), and the agent tracing guide sends users who are doing that to the "Trace LLM applications" guide instead [S1]. My inference from this: the Agents view only fills in when your code records conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool calls as agent data.

**How the Agents view works**
- It models the agent, the conversation that groups turns, each user-agent exchange (a "turn"), the LLM calls inside a turn, and the tool calls those LLM calls trigger [S1].
- Each of these is sent as an OpenTelemetry *span* (a record of one operation). Each span is tagged with attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id` [S1].

**Ways to get there**
1. **Built-in integrations:** Install a plugin for your agent harness, or call `weave.init()` in code that uses a supported agent SDK. Weave then patches the framework automatically. Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own. With agent SDKs, your code decides which turns belong together, so `weave.init()` alone isn't enough [S2].
2. **Custom agents:** Use the Weave SDK's agent helpers directly, or point an existing OTel pipeline at Weave [S4].

**Minimal custom setup** (call `weave.init()` first; without it, the agent functions silently do nothing [S6]):

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent") as conversation:
    with conversation.start_turn(user_message="[USER-MESSAGE]") as turn:
        with weave.start_llm(model="[MODEL]", provider_name="[PROVIDER]") as llm:
            llm.output("[ASSISTANT-REPLY]")
```

This follows the documented pattern. Each helper works as a context manager, and Weave keeps the active conversation and turn in context, so nested functions can call `start_llm()` or `start_tool()` without passing them around [S3, S5].

## Multi-turn conversations

Bedrock Agents preserve conversation state on the service side when you reuse a `sessionId`. To group multiple turns into a single trace in the Weights & Biases UI, wrap the turns in `weave.thread`:

```python lines theme={"system"}
with weave.thread("support-conversation") as t:
    for prompt in [
        "I can't log in to my account.",
        "I already tried resetting my password.",
    ]:
        ask_agent(prompt, session_id=t.thread_id)
```

Weave displays each turn in the UI as individual rows in the Threads view.

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

input.answer:
No. `@weave.op` alone won't give you the Agents view. The docs treat `@weave.op` as a separate workflow: it traces individual functions as Ops (tracked function calls), and the agent tracing guide sends users who are doing that to the "Trace LLM applications" guide instead [S1]. My inference from this: the Agents view only fills in when your code records conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool calls as agent data.

**How the Agents view works**
- It models the agent, the conversation that groups turns, each user-agent exchange (a "turn"), the LLM calls inside a turn, and the tool calls those LLM calls trigger [S1].
- Each of these is sent as an OpenTelemetry *span* (a record of one operation). Each span is tagged with attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id` [S1].

**Ways to get there**
1. **Built-in integrations:** Install a plugin for your agent harness, or call `weave.init()` in code that uses a supported agent SDK. Weave then patches the framework automatically. Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own. With agent SDKs, your code decides which turns belong together, so `weave.init()` alone isn't enough [S2].
2. **Custom agents:** Use the Weave SDK's agent helpers directly, or point an existing OTel pipeline at Weave [S4].

**Minimal custom setup** (call `weave.init()` first; without it, the agent functions silently do nothing [S6]):

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent") as conversation:
    with conversation.start_turn(user_message="[USER-MESSAGE]") as turn:
        with weave.start_llm(model="[MODEL]", provider_name="[PROVIDER]") as llm:
            llm.output("[ASSISTANT-REPLY]")
```

This follows the documented pattern. Each helper works as a context manager, and Weave keeps the active conversation and turn in context, so nested functions can call `start_llm()` or `start_tool()` without passing them around [S3, S5].

input.answer:
No. `@weave.op` alone won't give you the Agents view. The docs treat `@weave.op` as a separate workflow: it traces individual functions as Ops (tracked function calls), and the agent tracing guide sends users who are doing that to the "Trace LLM applications" guide instead [S1]. My inference from this: the Agents view only fills in when agent data is actually sent. That means conversations, turns, LLM calls and tool calls carrying GenAI semantic-convention attributes, sent by an integration, by the agent helpers, or through OpenTelemetry (OTel) [S2, S4].

**How the Agents view works**
- It models the agent, the conversation that groups turns, each user-agent exchange (a "turn"), the LLM calls inside a turn, and the tool calls those LLM calls trigger [S1].
- Every turn, LLM call and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a record of one operation). Spans are tagged with attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id` [S1].

**Ways to get there**
1. **Built-in integrations:** Install a plugin for your agent harness, or call `weave.init()` in code that uses a supported agent SDK. Weave then patches the framework automatically. Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own. With agent SDKs, your code decides which turns belong together, so `weave.init()` alone isn't enough [S2].
2. **Custom agents:** Use the Weave SDK's agent helpers directly, or point an existing OTel pipeline at Weave [S4].

**Minimal custom setup** (call `weave.init()` first; without it, the agent functions silently do nothing [S6]). This is adapted from the documented context-manager example [S5]:

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent") as conversation:
    with conversation.start_turn(user_message="[USER-MESSAGE]") as turn:
        with weave.start_llm(model="[MODEL]", provider_name="[PROVIDER]") as llm:
            llm.output("[ASSISTANT-REPLY]")
```

Each helper works as a context manager. Weave keeps the active conversation and turn in context, so nested functions can call `start_llm()` or `start_tool()` without passing them around [S3, S5].
